summary: Defines encoding instructions that can be added to an ASN.1 specification to change how values are encoded by RXER and its canonical form, such as encoding a component as an XML attribute rather than a child element. It is an experimental protocol.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 4911 lets an ASN.1 specification carry instructions that change the XML it produces. An instruction can say that one field should be written as an XML attribute, that a list should be written as values separated by spaces, or that a definition in another XML schema language should be reused as it is.

subtitle: Annotations that change how an ASN.1 specification is turned into XML, without changing the values it defines.

tldr.problem: A protocol described in ASN.1 has one natural XML shape, but XML schemas, DTDs and RELAX NG all describe data differently, so an ASN.1 specification cannot easily reuse definitions written in them.
tldr.mechanism: The memo defines encoding instructions that are written into an ASN.1 specification and that tell the Robust XML Encoding Rules how to encode particular components, for example to write a component as an XML attribute instead of a child element.
tldr.outcome: It is an Experimental document, and a companion to the RXER specification. The effects of each instruction are described fully in RXER and in ASN.X rather than in this memo.

facts.label: XML schema languages referenced
facts.value: XML Schema, RELAX NG and DTD

today: RFC 4911 is an Experimental document from July 2007, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It is a companion to the RXER specification, which defines the Robust XML Encoding Rules themselves, and to the ASN.X specification. The memo states that the precise effect of each encoding instruction is described fully in those specifications rather than in this one.

sections.title: Introduction and Purpose
sections.content:
The memo defines encoding instructions that may be used in an ASN.1 specification to alter how ASN.1 values are encoded by the Robust XML Encoding Rules and by the Canonical Robust XML Encoding Rules. An example given in the abstract is encoding a component of an ASN.1 value as an XML attribute rather than as a child element. Some of the instructions also affect how an ASN.1 specification is translated into an Abstract Syntax Notation X specification.

The memo also defines encoding instructions that allow an ASN.1 specification to incorporate the definitions of types, elements and attributes in specifications written in other XML schema languages. References to XML Schema types, elements and attributes, to RELAX NG named patterns and elements, and to XML document type definition element types are supported.

The memo is candid about its own scope. In most cases the effect of an encoding instruction is only briefly mentioned in the document; the precise effects are described fully in the specifications for RXER and for ASN.X, at the points where they apply. The encoding reference that identifies the Robust XML Encoding Rules is literally RXER, and an RXER encoding instruction applies equally to both RXER and CRXER encodings.

Throughout the memo, type means an ASN.1 type and value means an ASN.1 abstract value, unless qualified otherwise. A reference to an ASN.1 production is a reference to text in an ASN.1 specification corresponding to that production, and component is synonymous with NamedType. The example ASN.1 definitions in the memo are assumed to be defined in a module with a TagDefault of AUTOMATIC TAGS and an EncodingReferenceDefault of RXER INSTRUCTIONS.
sections.plainLanguage: ASN.1 describes data in its own way, and XML has several ways of describing data. This memo is the bridge: it adds small instructions to an ASN.1 specification that say how the XML should look.

sections.title: The Notation for RXER Encoding Instructions
sections.content:
The grammar of ASN.1 permits the application of encoding instructions, through type prefixes and encoding control sections, that modify how abstract values are encoded by nominated encoding rules. The generic notation for type prefixes and encoding control sections is defined by the ASN.1 basic notation and includes an encoding reference to identify the specific encoding rules affected. The specific notation for an encoding instruction is left to the specification of those encoding rules, so this memo, as a companion to the RXER specification, defines the notation for RXER encoding instructions. It elaborates the EncodingInstruction and EncodingInstructionAssignmentList placeholder productions of the ASN.1 basic notation.

The EncodingInstruction production admits sixteen alternatives, one for each kind of instruction: attribute, attribute reference, component reference, element reference, group, insertions, list, name, reference as element, reference as type, simple content, type as version, type reference, union, values and version indicator. The EncodingInstructionAssignmentList production, which appears only in an encoding control section, admits a schema identity instruction, a target namespace instruction and top-level components.

The memo defines what a top-level NamedType is: it is a NamedType that appears in a TopLevelComponent, and a NamedType nested within the type of a top-level component is not itself top level. The memo warns that non-trivial types defined within a top-level NamedType will not be visible to ASN.1 tools that do not understand RXER. Each top-level NamedType within a module must have a distinct identifier.

The instructions draw on four value productions, NCNameValue, AnyURIValue, QNameValue and NameValue, whose governing types are the NCName, AnyURI, QName and Name types from the AdditionalBasicDefinitions module of the RXER specification. A value in one of these must not be a dummy reference and must not textually contain a nested dummy reference. The memo draws the consequence: encoding instructions are not permitted to be parameterized in any way.
sections.plainLanguage: Each instruction has its own keyword and its own shape of argument, written into the ASN.1 source in a type prefix. An encoding control section at the top of the module can also declare the module's identity, its namespace and its top-level components.

sections.title: Changing How Values Are Encoded
sections.content:
The instructions fall into groups. The component encoding instructions are ATTRIBUTE, ATTRIBUTE-REF, COMPONENT-REF, GROUP, ELEMENT-REF, NAME, REF-AS-ELEMENT, SIMPLE-CONTENT, TYPE-AS-VERSION and VERSION-INDICATOR. The reference encoding instructions are ATTRIBUTE-REF, COMPONENT-REF, ELEMENT-REF, REF-AS-ELEMENT, REF-AS-TYPE and TYPE-REF. These let an ASN.1 specification incorporate definitions from other XML schema languages, through implied constraints on the markup that may appear in values of the Markup type or of UTF8String.

The ATTRIBUTE instruction causes an RXER encoder to encode a value of the component as an XML attribute instead of as a child element. Its base type must not be a CHOICE, SET or SET OF, must not be a SEQUENCE other than the one defining QName, must not be a SEQUENCE OF whose type is not subject to a LIST instruction, and must not be an open type. The ATTRIBUTE-REF instruction does the same but names the attribute after a referenced XML Schema attribute declaration or a top-level NamedType, and it restricts values of the UTF8String type to conform to the type of that declaration.

Several instructions change names or shapes. The NAME instruction makes the encoder use a nominated character string wherever the component's identifier would otherwise appear. The LIST instruction makes a value of a SEQUENCE OF type be encoded as a white-space-separated list of the component values, and the component type must have a base type such as BOOLEAN, INTEGER, ENUMERATED, REAL, OBJECT IDENTIFIER, GeneralizedTime or UTCTime, or one of NCName, AnyURI, Name or QName. The SIMPLE-CONTENT instruction encodes a component's value without wrapping it in a child element of its own; at most one component of a SEQUENCE or SET may use it, and if one does then all the other components must be attribute components. The VALUES instruction uses nominated names instead of the identifiers that would otherwise appear in the encoding of a BIT STRING, ENUMERATED or INTEGER value. The UNION instruction lets the alternatives of a CHOICE share an element name, with a precedence list deciding which one applies.
sections.plainLanguage: These instructions decide the shape of the XML. A field can become an attribute, a list can become values separated by spaces, a field can lose its own wrapper, and names can be replaced with names you choose. Some instructions exclude each other, so a component cannot be given two conflicting shapes.

sections.title: Referring to Other XML Schema Languages
sections.content:
The reference encoding instructions exist so that an ASN.1 specification can reuse definitions written in other XML schema languages. The ELEMENT-REF instruction causes a value of the component to be encoded as an element whose name is a qualified name of the referenced element declaration, and it restricts values of the Markup type to conform to that declaration's type. The referenced declaration must be an XML Schema element declaration, a RELAX NG element definition, or a top-level NamedType that is not subject to an ATTRIBUTE instruction.

The REF-AS-ELEMENT instruction encodes a value as an element whose name is the name of an external DTD subset element type declaration, and restricts Markup values to the content and attributes that declaration permits. The REF-AS-TYPE instruction does not change the element name but restricts Markup values to the content and attributes permitted by the nominated element type declaration. The TYPE-REF instruction restricts values of the Markup type to conform to a specific XML Schema named type, a RELAX NG named pattern or an ASN.1 defined type.

Two more instructions do not change an encoding at all but do change what the specification means. The SCHEMA-IDENTITY instruction associates a unique URI with the module, has no effect on an RXER encoder but does affect the translation into ASN.X, and the character string given by each such instruction must be distinct, so successive versions of a module each have a different schema identity URI. The TARGET-NAMESPACE instruction associates an XML namespace name with the type, object class, value, object and object set references defined in the module, and with each top-level NamedType in the RXER encoding control section. Two or more modules may have the same target namespace provided the expanded names of their top-level attribute components are distinct across all of them, the expanded names of their top-level element components are distinct, and their references are distinct in their category.

The COMPONENT-REF instruction provides a more direct way of referencing a top-level component, which the ASN.1 basic notation has no concept of. It states that a NamedType within a combining type definition is equivalent to a referenced top-level NamedType, either in the same module or in another module named in the reference.
sections.plainLanguage: These instructions let one specification point at definitions written somewhere else, in XML Schema, RELAX NG or a DTD, and say that those definitions describe the data. Two more instructions attach a name and a namespace to the whole module, which matters when the same specification has more than one version.

sections.title: Extensions, Grouping and Versioning
sections.content:
Using the GROUP instruction on components with extensible types can lead to situations where an unknown extension could be associated with more than one extension insertion point. The insertion encoding instructions remove this ambiguity by limiting the form that extensions can take. Forward compatibility means the ability for a decoder to decode an encoding that contains extensions introduced in a more recent version of the specification than the one the decoder uses.

In the most general case an extension to a CHOICE, SET or SEQUENCE type generates zero or more attributes and zero or more elements. The MULTIFORM-INSERTIONS instruction says the encodings produced by forward-compatible extensions always consist of one or more elements and zero or more attributes, with no restriction on the names of the elements. The UNIFORM-INSERTIONS instruction says they always consist of one or more elements having the same expanded name, though that name may differ between encodings. The SINGULAR-INSERTIONS instruction says they always consist of a single element and zero or more attributes. The HOLLOW-INSERTIONS instruction says they always consist of zero elements and zero or more attributes. The NO-INSERTIONS instruction says no forward-compatible extensions can be made to the type at all. These instructions state what kinds of extensions are possible without breaking forward compatibility, but they do not prohibit extensions that do break it, and if such an extension is made then a new value should be introduced for a version indicator attribute whose scope covers it.

The VERSION-INDICATOR instruction provides a way to alert decoders that an encoding contains extensions that break forward compatibility. A NamedType subject to it must also be subject to an ATTRIBUTE instruction, and its type must be an extensible constrained type where each value represents a different version of the specification. Ordinarily an application sets the value of the version indicator attribute to be the last of the permitted values.

The GROUP instruction causes a value of the component to be encoded without encapsulation as an element, and it allows the construction of non-trivial content models for element content. The base type must be a SEQUENCE, SET or SET OF, a CHOICE not subject to a UNION instruction, or a SEQUENCE OF not subject to a LIST instruction. Section 25.1 imposes further conditions on unambiguous encodings, on unique component attribution and on deterministic grammars.
sections.plainLanguage: When a specification is extended later, a decoder using an older version has to know how to read the new parts. These instructions say what shape an extension may take so that it stays readable. The grouping instruction lets a set of fields share a parent element instead of each having its own, and the version indicator lets a decoder be told that it is looking at something newer than it expected.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The memo says ASN.1 compiler implementors should take special care to be thorough in checking that the GROUP encoding instruction has been used correctly, because otherwise specifications with ambiguous RXER encodings could be deployed.

Ambiguous encodings mean that the abstract value recovered by a decoder may differ from the original abstract value that was encoded. If that happens, a digital signature generated with respect to the original abstract value, using a canonical encoding other than CRXER, will not be successfully verified by a receiver using the decoded abstract value. An abstract value may also have security-sensitive fields, in particular fields used to grant or deny access, so if the decoded abstract value differs from the encoded one, a receiver using the decoded value will be applying different security policy than the original value embodies.
sections.plainLanguage: Misusing the grouping instruction can make two different values decode to the same thing. That matters for security, because a signature made over the original value would then fail to check, and because a field that decides whether access is granted might read differently on the two sides.

items.title: ATTRIBUTE
items.text: Write the component as an XML attribute instead of a child element.

items.title: ATTRIBUTE-REF
items.text: The same, but the attribute is named after a referenced XML Schema attribute declaration.

items.title: ELEMENT-REF
items.text: Write the component as an element named after a referenced element declaration, and restrict Markup values to it.

items.title: REF-AS-ELEMENT and REF-AS-TYPE
items.text: Reference an element type declaration in an external DTD subset.

items.title: NAME
items.text: Use a nominated name wherever the component's identifier would appear.

items.title: LIST
items.text: Write a SEQUENCE OF value as a white-space-separated list of the component values.

items.title: SIMPLE-CONTENT
items.text: Write the component's value without a child element of its own.

items.title: VALUES
items.text: Use nominated names for BIT STRING, ENUMERATED or INTEGER values.
